query: What review signals predict negative Amazon product satisfaction?

per_column.name: defect_type
per_column.rationale: Categorising the nature of a product defect is a strong analytical axis for predicting negative satisfaction. Values are grounded: the doll review is reasonably 'missing_or_incomplete', and books/music with no product defect are correctly 'not_present'. Distribution is skewed to 'not_present' but that is a warranted silent value, not a flaw.

per_column.name: expectation_gap
per_column.rationale: Whether the product met/fell below expectations is directly relevant to satisfaction prediction and gives a good grouping axis. Most mappings are sound (Lamott book 'quality_below_expectations', Bicycle Thieves 'met_expectations'). The doll review as 'description_mismatch' is a slight stretch but defensible; skincare 'better_than_expected' is reasonable.

per_column.name: sentiment_intensity
per_column.rationale: A 1-5 intensity scale is derivable from text tone and is more granular than a bare sentiment flag, so it carries some leverage. However it is largely a proxy/restatement of the outcome (satisfaction) the query targets, risking circularity and redundancy with label_pos, capping usefulness. Sample values track sentiment sensibly.

per_column.name: reviewer_use_context
per_column.rationale: Use context (gift, child, professional) is a legitimate new segmentation axis for satisfaction analysis. Values are well grounded: doll for daughter -> 'child_or_family', skincare -> 'personal_use', silent reviews -> 'not_present'. Mostly silent but that is warranted.

per_column.name: product_category_signal
per_column.rationale: Product category is a useful axis to compare dissatisfaction drivers across media vs physical goods. Values are soundly inferred from content (book, music, film, physical product), matching the source text well.

judge.rationale: The added columns provide several genuine new axes (defect type, expectation gap, use context, category) that support predicting negative satisfaction, all well grounded in the source text with appropriate 'not_present' handling for silent rows and no observed hallucinations. sentiment_intensity is the weakest, partly restating the target outcome, but the set overall is analytically useful and faithful to the source.
